h: How to Win (or at Least Not Lose Badly)
p: Bowling looks easy until you try it in front of your mates. So here's a crash course. Choose a ball that fits your hand comfortably and that you can control. Line up with the arrows on the lane rather than staring at the pins, take a smooth approach, release the ball low and follow through towards your target. Don't step over the foul line, or that shot doesn't count.

Scoring is simple once you get it. A strike, all ten pins down with your first ball, earns ten plus your next two balls. A spare, clearing the rest on your second go, gets ten plus your next ball. Three strikes in a row is a turkey, and the perfect game is 300.

With St James' Park so close, matchday is a big deal around here. If Newcastle are at home, the area fills up with fans before and after the game, so plan around kick-off if you want a calmer evening, or lean into the atmosphere and book a post-match lane to celebrate or drown your sorrows.

Elsewhere in the city, the Discovery Museum is just down the road and tells the story of Tyneside's industry and innovation, including Turbinia, the record-breaking steam-turbine ship. It's free to visit and a cracking way to spend a couple of hours before a night at the lanes.
